E1.title: Laura Robson
section_path: 2012: First WTA Tour final, Olympic mixed doubles silver medalist

E3.title: Laura Robson
E3.text: In July 2015, she played at the 50k event in Granby and won a tough three-set match over second seed Naomi Osaka.

E4.title: Laura Robson
E4.text: However, she lost her next match to American qualifier Ellie Halbauer.

E5.title: Laura Robson
E5.text: Robson also reached the final in doubles partnering Erin Routliffe.

E6.title: Laura Robson
E6.text: In Gatineau, she retired from her first-round match, generating fear that her wrist injury had returned, but Robson said that she had been hampered by a stomach strain she had suffered during practice.

E7.title: Laura Robson
E7.text: Robson played left-handed, with a two-handed backhand.

E8.title: Laura Robson
E8.text: One of her strengths was her "dominant" serve.

E9.title: Laura Robson
E9.text: She had a strong game from the back of the court and was also noted for having an aggressive forehand return.

E10.title: Laura Robson
E10.text: However, she has been criticised for having "poor lateral movement", as well as an inconsistent second serve, resulting in a considerable number of double faults.

E11.title: Laura Robson
E11.text: She has been praised for showing "extraordinary poise", and having "the attitude and technique required of a leading player".

E12.title: Laura Robson
E12.text: Commentator Simon Reed said that she "has every tool she needs", and former Grand Slam champion Pat Cash called her "a special talent" who "seems to have all the attributes to progress".

E13.title: Laura Robson
E13.text: Former WTA player Ana Ivanovic said that Robson "hits the ball really, really hard", former top British player Samantha Smith said that "she doesn't have any weaknesses at all", and Serena Williams stated that Robson is an "all-around good player".

E14.title: Laura Robson
E14.text: After the Australian Open, Robson did not play again until the start of April.

E15.title: Laura Robson
E15.text: In her third tournament back, she made the semifinal losing to Edina Gallovits of the ITF event in Dothan, after having to qualify for the main draw.

E16.title: Laura Robson
E16.text: She also played in the doubles, and after reaching the quarterfinals, she reached a career high of No.

E18.title: Laura Robson
E18.text: She followed this up with a quarterfinal appearance in Charlottesville losing to Anastasiya Yakimova.

E19.title: Laura Robson
E19.text: Laura Robson (born 21 January 1994) is a British former professional tennis player.

E20.title: Laura Robson
E20.text: She debuted on the ITF Junior Circuit in 2007, and a year later won the Junior Wimbledon championships at the age of 14.

E21.title: Laura Robson
E21.text: As a junior, she also twice reached the final of the girls' singles tournament at the Australian Open, in 2009 and 2010.

E22.title: Laura Robson
E22.text: She won her first tournament on the ITF Women's Circuit in November 2008.

E23.title: Laura Robson
E23.text: Due to her focusing on her senior career, Robson entered the US Open unseeded.

E24.title: Laura Robson
E24.text: In the first round, she beat Ons Jabeur of Tunisia.

E25.title: Laura Robson
E25.text: She then faced the seventh seed Lauren Embree of the United States and beat her in three sets.

E26.title: Laura Robson
E26.text: She went on to face the 12th seed, Tamaryn Hendler, who she defeated in straight sets.

E27.title: Laura Robson
E27.text: Robson then beat Lauren Davis in the quarterfinals.

E28.title: Laura Robson
E28.text: In her semifinal, she faced Yana Buchina of Russia.

E29.title: Laura Robson
E29.text: Due to rain delay, both quarter- and semifinals were played on the same day.

E30.title: Laura Robson
E30.text: Therefore, the semifinal followed the quarterfinal match.

E31.title: Laura Robson
E31.text: Despite starting strongly, Robson tired, losing the match in three sets.

E33.title: Laura Robson
E33.text: According to her parents, she began playing tennis "as soon as she could hold a tennis racquet", and after being encouraged by them, she entered a junior tennis academy at age seven.

E34.title: Laura Robson
E34.text: She signed with management company Octagon when she was ten, with Adidas at age 11, and also signed a racquet deal with Wilson Sporting Goods.

E35.title: Laura Robson
E35.text: Following her victory at Wimbledon, Robson made her debut on the ITF Women's Circuit at a $10k tournament in Limoges, France.

E36.title: Laura Robson
E36.text: She won two matches to qualify for the main draw of the tournament, as well as her first-round match, before having to retire with a shoulder injury in the second round against the second seed Marina Melnikova.

E37.title: Laura Robson career statistics
E37.text: Over her career, Robson has claimed one ITF title.

E38.title: Laura Robson career statistics
E38.text: On the ITF Junior Circuit, she won the Wimbledon Championships in 2008 and finished runner-up at the Australian Open 2009 and 2010.

E39.title: Laura Robson
E39.text: Robson started her 2014 season at the Hobart International, where she had to retire in her first-round match against Yanina Wickmayer due to a left wrist injury.

E40.title: Laura Robson
E40.text: Her wrist continued to affect her at the Australian Open, where Kirsten Flipkens defeated her in straight sets.

E41.title: Laura Robson
E41.text: After taking three-months rest from the tour, Robson underwent surgery on her left wrist in April.

E42.title: Laura Robson
E42.text: The surgery forced her to miss the French Open, Wimbledon and the US Open, and although Robson initially hoped to be playing by the end of the season, she only started training in October, and did not play again in 2014.

E43.title: Laura Robson
E43.text: After a brief period on the main tour, Robson returned to junior competition but was knocked out in the second round of a tournament in December.

E44.title: Laura Robson
E44.text: In the same month she played her final junior tournament of 2008, the Orange Bowl, where she had to retire in the third round with a stomach strain.

E45.title: Laura Robson
E45.text: At the end of the year, she was shortlisted for the BBC Young Sports Personality of the Year, but lost out to Paralympic swimmer Eleanor Simmonds.
